question: Which Magic: The Gathering Standard card (non-foil paper version released in its original set) that was banned at the same time as Oko, Thief of Crowns (including Oko, Crown of Thorns) had the highest price decrease from its all-time high to its all-time low?

history.name: MTG_StandardFormatHistory_Expert
history.content:
Task restatement: Determine which Standard card banned on the same date as Oko, Thief of Crowns (note: "Oko, Crown of Thorns" appears to be a typographical confusion and will be treated as Oko, Thief of Crowns) had the greatest price drop (non-foil, paper, original set) from all-time high to all-time low.
Plan:
- Confirm the Standard ban date for Oko and enumerate all cards banned on that announcement.
- Confirm original sets and that non-foil, paper versions exist.
- Have the price specialist compile all-time high and low for each card (original set, non-foil, paper only).
- Compute absolute drop = high - low and identify the maximum.
- Validate using an independent check.
Proceeding to the ban date and co-banned cards.

mistake_reason: The Validation_Expert approved the result using only a superficial "sanity check" that verified numeric types, positivity, and high > low, without cross-checking against authoritative external price histories. They treated internal arithmetic consistency as sufficient validation and declared the values plausible, failing to detect that the compiled highs and lows were incorrect (notably understating Oko's true all-time high). This is an FM-3.3 Incorrect Verification error: applying a defective verification test that inevitably passes regardless of actual data quality, leading to a false confirmation and the wrong final answer.
